title: Drive a started spring pin through a clevis hub and shaft with a pin punch and hammer until neither end stands proud
instruction: Pin the shaft to the clevis.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, 1.62 million employed) have as a core task 'Repair machines, equipment, or structures, using tools such as hammers...'; spring pins lock hubs, gears, collars and clevises to shafts throughout machinery, and team assemblers (1.4 million) fit them on lines. A started pin is held only by friction: one hand keeps a roll-pin punch's pilot in its end and the punch square while the other strikes. Off square, the pin cocks and binds; a hammer face that reaches the hub dents it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Steel V-block 7.5 (x) x 6 x 6 cm with a 90 deg V 4 cm wide at the top and a 4 mm relief slot, x 26.3 to 33.8, y -3 to 3, clamped (fixed). In its V lies the hub of a steel clevis: hub 24 mm across and 30 mm long along x, 12 mm bore, its fork (two 6 mm ears, 8 mm clevis pin) pointing toward the robot (x 23.5 to 26.5). A 12 mm steel shaft fills the bore and runs 12 cm out along +x (to x 41.5). Hub and shaft are cross-drilled 4 mm on one vertical axis at x 28.0, y 0.0; the hub's top is 6.9 cm above the table. In that hole a 4 x 22 mm steel slotted spring pin (ISO 8752, 1.4 g) is started 3.0 mm and stands 19.0 mm proud. Loose on the table: a 5/32 in roll-pin punch (steel: 4 mm point 40 mm long ending in a 1.8 mm rounded pilot that fits the pin's 2.4 mm open end, 9.6 mm body, 100 mm long, 36 g) lying along the line from the left arm's base toward the hole, its point at (10.8, 18.7) toward the left arm, its head at (17.6, 11.3); a Vaughan TC308 8 oz ball-peen hammer (steel head 85 mm with a 22 mm face, hickory handle 15 x 24 mm, 298 mm long, 0.37 kg) lying on its side, its head at (12.2, -11.9), its handle running to (33.4, -31.3). Distractors, loose, ignored by the scorer: a cotton shop rag (26 x 23 cm, 50 g) at (47, 25); a can of multi-purpose oil (steel, 5.2 x 10.4 x 27.2 cm, 0.45 kg) at (50, -27); an M16 steel hex nut (24 mm across flats, 30 g) at (44, 8). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The pin's depth d is how far its lower end is below the top of the 24 mm hub (it starts at 3.0 mm; the 22 mm pin's upper end then stands 22 - d mm proud of the hub and its lower end d - 24 mm proud of the hub's underside). 1.0: neither end proud by more than 0.25 mm (d from 21.75 to 24.25 mm), no blow recorded on the part and the pin not cocked, every fingertip of both grippers at least 5 cm from the top of the hole, the punch's point at least 3 cm from the pin, no part of the hammer within 2 cm of the hub and the pin at rest, all held for 3 s. 0.75: neither end proud as above, but the hands or tools not yet clear. 0.5: the pin through the shaft and at least 2 mm into the hub's far wall (d at least 20 mm). 0.25: the pin through the hub's near wall and at least 2 mm into the shaft (d at least 8 mm). Otherwise 0; doing nothing leaves d at 3 mm and scores 0. A blow on the part or a cocked pin caps the score at 0.25 for the rest of the run. A blow on the part is any part of the hammer touching the clevis, hub or shaft while moving at 0.1 m/s or more, the punch being struck while its point rests on the hub and not on the pin, or the hammer's face driving the pin to within 0.5 mm of flush. The pin cocks when the punch is struck while its axis is more than 3 deg off the hole's or its point is 1.6 to 3 mm off the pin's centre (less than half of it on the pin's end), or when the face strikes the pin directly more than 3 deg off square. Real trial: d and both protrusions with a depth gauge or a steel rule and straightedge; blows on the part as bright marks on the layout-blued hub and shaft.
reset_notes: A driven pin is not reused. Between trials drive it out from below through the V-block's relief slot with the same punch, wipe and re-blue the hub and shaft (layout fluid), line up the holes with a 4 mm drill blank, start a new 4 x 22 mm pin by hand with one light tap and check with a depth gauge that it stands 19.0 mm proud (within 0.3 mm). Lay the punch and hammer back on their tape marks.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The pin's grip in the bores is a model: it moves only on a blow at 0.3 m/s or more, each blow driving it until 5 N per mm of engaged pin has absorbed the hammer's energy (scaled: simulated blows carry about 0.13 J, real ones more). Cocking and marking are rules, not deformation. Clevis, shaft, V-block, punch and hammer are primitives (the SimReady hammer is one SDF mesh that cannot be gripped and struck); rag, oil can and nut are SimReady props.
